📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Turn off reality TV and turn on the bald eagle cams. It’s all the drama you need.

Sources indicate that when internet-famous bald eagle Shadow seemingly welcomed a mysterious latest female into his nest earlier this week, many fans have questioned the whereabouts of Kaydee. After the death of Shadow’s longtime partner Jackie in August, he had been spotted spending time with the 4-year-old banded female eagle named KD1 (later renamed Kaydee). It seemed like the eagles might head into mating season as a pair, but after the arrival of a new, large female, it’s unclear how the relationships will all shake out.

Since the appearance of the mystery female, nicknamed Major Beautiful Visitor or BBV by some fans, Kaydee has disappeared from view of Friends of Big Bear Valley (FOBBV)’s two cameras. She was last spotted by the cameras on November 14 in the Roost Tree, according to FOBBV. Despite concerns that she may be injured or had left the area, wildlife photographers have continued to document Kaydee’s presence near Big Bear Lake as recently as November 18.

According to recent reports, photographer Alla Shumko shared photos of Kaydee perched near Big Bear Lake on November 18. Kaydee’s double bands are visible as she observed a scuffle between younger eagles fighting over fish.

It has been revealed that mating season is well underway, so viewers of FOBBV’s 24/7 livecams have been watching closely for signs that Shadow has selected a upcoming partner. Shadow has worked with both Kaydee and the new eagle on nest maintenance and shared “beaky kisses” with each female, both signs of bonding in bald eagles. Bald eagle mating involves a bit of aerial acrobatics—copulating pairs can be seen in what’s called a “cartwheel display,” in which they lock talons in mid-air while tumbling down to the ground. Male eagles do not have an external phallus, so mating occurs via a touch of cloacas. Vocalizations can typically be heard during the act, which lasts about 7 to 12 seconds, according to Raptor Resource.

As this is nature, we humans can’t predict or influence who Shadow will pick as a latest partner. Or if he picks at all. All we can do is watch and wait and let nature take its course.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In the shop’s new video, “The First Ever Electric Bel Air,” founder and CEO Ryan Friedlinghaus explains that a longtime client, Troy Swope, wants to convert an entire car collection to electric and picked the Bel Air to go first.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that west Coast Customs has finished its first electric Chevy Bel Air, and there’s not much Chevy left under the paint. The Burbank shop cut the body off a Tesla Model 3, kept the entire rolling platform, and set a 1955 Bel Air shell on top of it.

The result, called Project B-Zero, looks like a ’55 Chevy from the curb and like a Model 3 as soon as you open the door. And it charges at Tesla Superchargers.

In the shop’s new video, “The First Ever Electric Bel Air,” founder and CEO Ryan Friedlinghaus explains that a longtime client, Troy Swope, wants to convert an entire car collection to electric and picked the Bel Air to go first. WCC had previously built the same client a Chevelle with a big gas engine.

Industry observers note that friedlinghaus, who drives a Tesla himself, decided against pulling the Model 3’s motors and battery out and fitting them into the old Chevy. Instead, the Tesla stays whole and the Chevy becomes the body kit.

Sources indicate that that’s a formula WCC has used for years with gas cars. The shop calls it “old school meets new school”: an old GTO body on a new GTO, an old Camaro on a new Camaro, an old Mustang on a new Mustang. B-Zero is the first time it did it with a Tesla underneath.

“It sounds easy, but that process was tedious,” Friedlinghaus remarked.

Recent findings suggest that before any Chevy sheet metal went on, the crew took the bare Model 3 skateboard for a spin on the streets around the shop, with no doors, no lights and no seatbelts. Friedlinghaus joked about how many safety violations they were racking up. But it drove fine.

The real headache was the wheelbase. A 1955 Chevy rides on a 115-inch wheelbase, while the Model 3 sits at 113.2 inches. On its gas builds, WCC can cut, shorten or lengthen the newer car’s frame to match the old body. You can’t do that with a Tesla, since the floor is the battery pack.

So the shop changed the body instead, stretching the Bel Air’s rear wheel wells so the wheels sit where they look like they belong.

According to recent reports, the client wanted the exterior to read as a mostly stock Bel Air. The original car was red, so WCC kept it red, with a satin finish and gloss black accents.

Industry observers note that inside, it’s a Model 3. The shop kept the Tesla’s interior, including the steering wheel and center touchscreen, and modified it to fit the Chevy body. The seats got black suede with white stitching in an octagon pattern that Friedlinghaus stated was borrowed from the Lamborghini Urus, plus red accents and a “B-Zero” script on the dash.

Industry observers note that friedlinghaus stated the goal was for people to see “a really nice Bel Air” from the outside, then open the door and find a Tesla. He also expects some double takes when it pulls into a Supercharger station.

It has been revealed that he admits the reaction has been split. Plenty of people are mad that the shop electrified a Bel Air, and plenty of others think it came out great. The client is clearly in the second camp, describing the car as easy to drive and saying every trip in it feels like an event.

Here’s the full build video from West Coast Customs:.

This is sick. I know Tesla doesn’t care about personal car ownership anymore, but they should really sell their platform so shops can do these conversions without using salvage vehicles.

Well I was really interested in this build until I read how they kept it entirely Tesla inside. Not at all what I was thinking or what I'd call a true old car conversion to EV. Instead, they simply transformed the outside of a Tesla into an old looking car. To me, even the outside looks too far removed from the original Bel Air and more like a street rod. If that's what the owner wants and paid for, great.

But for me, I would never do a conversion like that. I really want to convert an older 70's or 80's or early 90's Cadillac into an EV. But for me, I will insist that the outside and inside look 100% like the original car with just an EV powertrain.

Don’t get me wrong, if you can recycle a salvage, that’s good, but it can’t always be done.

Recent findings suggest that compare it to the 1966 Mustang that a Sacramento Tesla parts shop converted earlier this year. That project took about $40,000 and two years, with the team grafting sections of a Model 3 floor into the Mustang. It’s an amazing build, but it’s a lot of custom engineering. WCC’s approach skips most of that. You keep Tesla’s crash structure, battery thermal management, software, over-the-air updates and Supercharger access, because you never took the car apart in the first place. It’s closer to what S-Klub did with its Model 3-based Mercedes 300SL than a traditional drivetrain swap.

The purists will hate it. That’s fine. This Bel Air will get driven more in a year than most restored ones get driven in a decade.

  • If you're someone who loves a fresh manicure, especially one with some length, you know the struggle of keeping your tips intact at the gym.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Sources indicate that THE ENDORPHINS, the physical changes you can see and feel in your body, the overall confidence boost that comes with doing something good for your body—yeah, the benefits of working out are hard to beat. The one area where a sweat session can fall short, however, is when it comes to the health of our nails.

If you're someone who loves a fresh manicure, especially one with some length, you know the struggle of keeping your tips intact at the gym. Between chipped polish, cracks and peeling, and the mental gymnastics of trying to avoid both, it can sometimes feel like your nails (and your sanity) are getting a workout of their own. “When I’m lifting plates or handling weights, I’m always conscious of how I’m gripping,” shares celebrity manicurist and KISS ambassador Gina Edwards, who's a frequent gym-goer herself. “I use my finger pads rather than the tips of my fingers to help avoid putting unnecessary pressure on my nails.”.

Meet the experts: Gina Edwards is a celebrity manicurist and KISS ambassador. Dana Stern, MD, is a New York-based dermatologist who specializes in nail disorders. Marisa Garshick, MD, is a dermatologist based in New York City. Jin Soon Choi is a celebrity manicurist in New York City.

According to recent reports, not into manicures? Unfortunately, that doesn't mean you're completely off the hook. Even bare nails can take a beating: “The nail is a thousand times more absorptive of water than the skin,” states Latest York dermatologist Dana Stern, MD, who specializes in nail disorders. And because frequent handwashing and exposure to moisture often go hand in hand with working out, nails are subjected to expansion as they absorb water and contraction as they dry. “Repeated wet-dry cycles can contribute to splitting and peeling, particularly in people already prone to brittle nails,” Dr Stern adds.

But not to worry—you don’t have to choose between having polished digits and getting your fitness on. With a few smart habits, you can avoid all the pitfalls. Here’s how.

No matter how you choose to work out, there are plenty of ways your nails can suffer. And most of us don't even realize we're putting them in harm's way until it's too late. Maybe you're in a workout class, engaging in some friendly competition with your neighbor to see who can knock out their burpees the fastest, only to jam a nail as your hands hit the ground. Or perhaps the damage happens before you even break a sweat. Picture it: You're pulling on your most compressive pair of leggings when a nail snags on the fabric or, worse, bends backward and breaks.

Of course, some activities pose a more obvious risk than others. Exercises that involve “repetitive gripping, pressure, or friction, such as weightlifting, rock climbing, and certain types of strength training” can be especially hard on your nails, claims Marisa Garshick, MD, a dermatologist based in Upcoming York City.

Here are a few of the ways your workout routine might be doing a number on them:.

Handling dumbbells, weight plates, and other equipment can put pressure on nails, especially if they're long, dry, or already weak, states celebrity manicurist Jin Soon Choi.

Jamming a nail against a hard surface or repeatedly putting pressure on it can cause the nail plate to separate from the nail bed, a condition known as onycholysis. This can happen to natural nails, too, although extensions may create additional opportunities for snagging.

Sources indicate that when a falsie gets caught on something, it can even cause the underlying natural nail to lift from the nail bed, explains Dr. Stern. Depending on the extent of the damage, it can take months for a healthy fresh nail to grow in.

Frequent handwashing and exposure to harsh cleansers (including those used to wipe down gym equipment and alcohol-based hand sanitizers) can contribute to splitting and peeling, Dr. Stern adds.

Sources indicate that while running and cycling may be gentler on your hands, repeated pressure inside athletic shoes can cause bruising beneath the nail (known as a subungual hematoma), thickening, or even nail loss, explains Dr. Garshick.

In a recent development, the good news? Most workout-related nail damage is temporary, provided the nail matrix, which is responsible for nail growth, hasn't been damaged. But more serious injuries can have lasting consequences. A crush injury—heavy weight falling on a nail, for example—could cause permanent damage to the nail matrix, Dr. Stern says. Even when the damage isn't permanent, patience is key. According to Dr. Garshick, fingernails typically take three to six months to grow out, while toenails can take twelve to eighteen months.

It has been revealed that the goal isn't to give up your favorite workouts or your favorite manicures. A few tweaks to your nail-care routine and how you handle equipment can make all the difference.

Here's what the pros recommend to keep your nails looking and feeling their best.

This ultra-nourishing product delivers a healthy dose of barrier-repairing ceramides, hyaluronic acid, and niacinamide sans greasy residue.

Jinsoon Primrose + Honeysuckle Healing Cuticle Oil.

Choi recommends this product, from her own line, before bed to help maintain healthy nails and cuticles.

OPI Repair Mode Bond Building Nail Serum.

It has been revealed that you’ve heard of bond builders for hair, right? This is the same thing, but for nails. It promises longer, stronger nails in just four weeks.

It’s notable to keep in mind that Dr. Garshick notes not every nail change is workout-related. Persistent discoloration, thickening, or lifting can sometimes indicate a fungal infection, psoriasis, or another nail condition. A upcoming or changing dark streak, particularly one that doesn't grow out, should also be evaluated by a board-certified dermatologist.

At the end of the day, you don't have to choose between crushing your fitness goals and keeping your nails in good shape. In fact, Choi points out that exercise itself can actually be beneficial for nail health, as physical activity promotes healthy circulation, helping deliver oxygen and nutrients to the tissues responsible for nail growth.

It's the accidental injuries and repeated pressure that can cause problems, not the workouts themselves. With a few simple adjustments to your nail-care routine and a bit more awareness of how you're handling equipment, you can keep breaking a sweat without breaking a nail.

#75376. Breaking: Does Menopausal Hormone Therapy Lower Dementia Risk? Timing and Genetics May Hold the Answer

📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (797 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Healthline ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Does Menopausal Hormone Therapy Lower Dementia Risk? Timing and Genetics May Hold the Answer

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (797 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Women who have longer reproductive life spans or use menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) may have better brain health as they age, according to a newly introduced study.
  • The research, published November 4 in Neurology, found that longer lifetime exposure to estrogen was associated with fewer signs of damage to small blood vessels in the brain.
  • The findings could offer newly introduced insights into the relationship between estrogen and brain aging, particularly as women account for approximately two-thirds of Alzheimer’s disease cases worldwide.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Women who have longer reproductive life spans or use menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) may have better brain health as they age, according to a newly introduced study.

The research, published November 4 in Neurology, found that longer lifetime exposure to estrogen was associated with fewer signs of damage to small blood vessels in the brain.

The findings could offer newly introduced insights into the relationship between estrogen and brain aging, particularly as women account for approximately two-thirds of Alzheimer’s disease cases worldwide.

Researchers also found that certain associations between hormone therapy and brain health differed depending on whether women carried a genetic variant associated with an increased risk of Alzheimer’s disease.

However, the relationship between estrogen and brain health is complex. While the findings suggest that longer estrogen exposure may be associated with healthier brain aging, they do not establish that hormone therapy can prevent Alzheimer’s disease or dementia.

The researchers drew data from the Gothenburg H70-1944 Birth Cohort, a longitudinal study of 1,203 individuals born in 1944 who resided in Gothenburg, Sweden.

The final cohort included 352 cisgender women, with an average age of 70, who had no neurological disorders and reliable self-reported data on their estrogen exposure.

Individual estrogen exposure was measured through structured interviews. It included:.

The researchers used this information as a proxy for lifetime estrogen exposure, though the study didn’t measure actual hormone levels.

Participants were also given a brain MRI at baseline and then again at a 5-year follow-up.

Sources indicate that the researchers found that those with a longer reproductive span had a lower risk of small vessel disease (SVD). Participants with a longer reproductive life span had an 8% lower risk of having two or more signs of SVD. However, later menopause, rather than earlier menstruation, appeared to be the main driver of this association.

Those who used MHT also tended to have fewer signs of SVD and better microstructural integrity in the white matter.

In individuals who carried the APOE-ε4 variant, which increases a person’s risk of Alzheimer’s disease, MHT was associated with greater cortical thickness in brain regions vulnerable to Alzheimer’s disease. However, there was no association for those without this variant.

The researchers noted that longer estrogen exposure was associated with stable cortical thickness and white matter trajectories over time.

Dung Trinh, MD, internist at MemorialCare Medical Group and Chief Medical Officer of Healthy Brain Clinic in Irvine, CA, who wasn’t involved in the study, told Healthline that estrogen has several vital effects on the brain that may help support cognitive health.

It influences communication between brain cells, supports the brain’s ability to use glucose for energy, helps regulate neurotransmitters, and plays a role in maintaining healthy blood vessels and reducing inflammation and oxidative stress.

Sources indicate that “As estrogen levels decline during menopause, some of these protective effects may diminish. Replacing estrogen closer to the menopause transition could potentially help preserve some of these functions during a vulnerable period for brain health,” he stated. “While these findings are encouraging, MHT has not been proven to prevent Alzheimer’s disease or dementia.”.

Sherry Ross, MD, board certified OB/GYN and Women’s Health Expert at Providence Saint John’s Health Center in Santa Monica, CA, who also wasn’t involved in the study, agreed and noted, “Starting menopausal hormone therapy earlier in the menopause transition may help minimize some changes by supporting the brain during this period of hormonal fluctuation.”.

“There is growing interest in whether early estrogen therapy may also help reduce the long-term risk of Alzheimer’s disease, although more research is needed before we can establish that benefit,” she added.

Ross told Healthline that this research reinforces the importance of recognizing menopause as more than a reproductive or hormonal transition.

“We know that women are disproportionately affected by dementia and Alzheimer’s disease, and some women experience noticeable cognitive changes beginning in perimenopause,” she remarked. “If future research confirms that starting hormone therapy earlier can help protect long-term cognitive health, it could influence how we approach menopause treatment and encourage more proactive conversations between women and their healthcare providers.”.

“The goal should be to individualize treatment based on a woman’s symptoms, medical history, and overall health rather than taking a one-size-fits-all approach,” Ross added.

Trinh agreed that an individualized approach to menopause management is crucial.

Industry observers note that “This does not mean that every woman should start hormone therapy to prevent dementia. Instead, it highlights the importance of understanding which women might benefit, when treatment should begin, and which formulations are most appropriate,” he said. “Factors such as age, time since menopause, cardiovascular risk, metabolic health, family history, and potentially genetic factors may all help guide future recommendations.”.

“We still need stronger clinical evidence before changing current prescribing guidelines specifically for dementia prevention,” Trinh added.

#75375. Breaking: The 'Possibility Couple' Is a Gen Z Dating Trend

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1073 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: The 'Possibility Couple' Is a Gen Z Dating Trend

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1073 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 21, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • So, say you want to be one half of a power couple—you know, a romantic pairing where both of you are successful and influential like Beyoncé and Jay-Z or Mr.
  • According to recent reports, well, how about trying to be part of a "possibility couple" now?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 21, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

So, say you want to be one half of a power couple—you know, a romantic pairing where both of you are successful and influential like Beyoncé and Jay-Z or Mr. and Mrs. Incredible. But the problem is you are still early on in your own personal power trip—meaning that you yourself have not become successful yet. What then can you do?

According to recent reports, well, how about trying to be part of a "possibility couple" now? That's a pairing that's all about the P's—namely "potential," "possibilities", "prediction," "potent," and, yes, maybe "power" eventually. A "possibility couple" is one that doesn't have power per se at the present. But it's got the potential to become quite potent in the future. In other words, based on what you are seeing now, you predict that together you'll have lots of potent possibilities down the road.

It shouldn't be super-surprising that the "possibility couple" is central to Hinge's third annual Gen Z D.A.T.E. (Data, Advice, Trends, and Expertise) Report titled: “Dating While Dreaming Big.” Since Gen Zers are those born between 1997 and 2012, they are now no older than 29 and thus are mostly still in the fruitcake batter stages of their lives—still forming their identities and possibilities.

It has been revealed that the Hinge report hinged on surveys administered to the over 13,000 consumers of the dating app. The survey results did suggest that many Gen Z respondents are looking into the future when evaluating their present dating prospects. For example, 81 percent of Gen Z respondents felt that "ending up with their ideal partner would make achieving their ideal life more likely," and 67 percent "would prefer a partner who makes them feel hopeful and inspired over someone who simply fits the life they’re already building." This forward-oriented view seemed to be more present among the Gen Zers, with 76 percent of them vs. 65 percent of millennials saying that "when they imagine their ideal romantic partner, they’re also imagining the person they want to become.".

Recent findings suggest that none of these are terrible things. Thinking more about your future and playing more of a long game when dating can be good approaches. The opposite would be just considering the here and now and trying to satisfy your immediate urges, such as, "Sure, that person is a bit crazy but so, so hot, and I'm so, so horny." Focusing too much on the present when looking for a partner can be like buying a pair of low-riding skinny jeans and thinking, "I'm going to wear these for life.".

Sources indicate that when you think only about who you are right now, rather than who you might become, you could be destined for some D's—meaning dispute, despair, and potentially divorce. You could end up outgrowing the other person. Or the person could end up holding you back. So, yes, it does make sense to find a person who is more open to possibilities for both of you.

A seemingly substantial challenge, though, of finding a possibility pairing is having to P a lot—meaning predicting, projecting, and prognosticating. It's not like a potential power pairing, where you can simply say, "I got the power. Do you?" and find the answer to be "yes" in both of your eyes. Whether the two of you might last without an eventual power outage is a different story.

Sources indicate that with a "possibility couple, any potential projections are further complicated by having to prognosticate for not just one but both of you when you don't know each other very well. In fact, neither of you may even be that self-aware yet. Plus, as stock market investors, weather forecasters, and the makers of Crystal Pepsi, Segways, and Joker: Folie à Deux will tell you, predicting what will happen in the future is not easy.

In a recent development, sure, there are present-day signs. For example, someone right now in law school is very likely to become a lawyer in a few years. But that lawyer could easily one day say, "Forget the law. Bring on yarn bombing." And who knows what twists and turns life may bring, such as health challenges, unexpected people entering or exiting, workplace and industry overhauls, or encountering a life-changing piece of tiramisu. I have previously warned in "A Funny Bone to Pick" about the dangers of dating someone's potential future self rather than who the person currently is because that person may end up never changing.

According to recent reports, therefore, the best possibility might be to balance the present with the future. You can ask yourself the question that I've already posed for "A Funny Bone to Pick"—namely, are you stronger with or without the person? Look for qualities that potential partners already have that would project well into the future.

Recent findings suggest that one such quality is open-mindedness—being open to different possibilities and people. After all, you may become a very different person at least outwardly. So, beware of anyone who stereotypes, focuses too much on superficial things, and holds strong biases.

A second quality is adaptability—the ability to accommodate future changes, such as the two of you growing in different ways. Or is your potential partner more like a starched denim thong—rigid and inflexible in a way that's surely going to drive a wedge between you in the future?

Industry observers note that thirdly, do they even want you to succeed and have a true teammate mindset where they want their partner to be as potent as possible? Or must they outshine everyone, including you? Beware of the people who make themselves feel high by keeping those around them low.

In a recent development, finally, are they a match for what's inside you—your core, your core personality and values, what won't change over time? If the two of you are attracted to each other's hot legs, abs, job, wallet, memberships, pick-up lines, car, or cast-iron cookware, remember those things definitely change over time—with the possible exception of the cast-iron cookware.

By contrast, what allows for growth is having strong roots beneath the surface. If the two of you can connect those roots—those things that go beyond the superficial—then the resulting possibilities could be endless.

A POPULAR STRATEGY is to skip a dose for the holiday week. But doctors tend to recommend against this strategy.

Vijay Kasi, MD, PhD, cardiologist at Orlando Health states that you might even experience short-term changes in blood pressure and blood sugar spikes, which is really only a concern if you are diabetic. Now would missing one GLP-1 dose severely impact the heart? Not really.

A 2026 study found that any heart benefit from taking a GLP-1 disappears after two years. Those same people were linked to a 22 percent increased risk of stroke, heart attacks, and early death.

Sources indicate that but again, we’re talking about a week—not two years. So what’s wrong with resuming a day or two after the holiday? If you are still adamant about skipping a dose, resuming it immediately after is recommended. “If they ate a really large meal and then immediately took the medication, they may feel very uncomfortable,” says Mir Ali, MD, medical director of MemorialCare Surgical Weight Loss Center at Orange Coast Medical Center. “But if they wait 24 hours and the meal has moved through their system, then it probably won't be as problematic.”.

Sources indicate that the real concern doctors have is if people continue to delay their GLP-1 schedule for multiple weeks. Dr. Ali says people stop feeling the effects a week after they stop the medication because that’s how long it stays in your system. Appetite returns and so does food noise—the persistent and intrusive thoughts related to cravings or obsessing over how much food you ate. Ashley Koff, RD, author of Your Best Shot, says other challenges that may promote overeating are that you no longer have a delay in gastric emptying and an alteration or sheer lack of fullness signaling. “When you stop this medication abruptly you go from [constant] sustained hormone back to your own which works at best for 2 to 5 minutes when triggered by food,” she says.

While one day of eating more than usual won’t make a significant change to your health, Dr. Kasi says that some people do struggle to get back on track after the holidays end. “For a few people, it may be easy, but a vast majority trying to break away from their established regimen might have problems.”.

DOCTORS ARE GENERALLY against taking a smaller dose than usual because it is not included in FDA guidelines for how to safely and effectively use a GLP-1. “If a lower dose wasn't effective for you beforehand, it's not going to be effective for you right before a holiday either,” says Dr. Ali. “It’s similar to skipping a dose.”.

There is one exception. Dr. Ali notes people who have attained a healthy weight or reached their goal weight may be able to lower their dose or take it less frequently as a maintenance strategy.

Industry observers note that “For some people who have been on it for a long time, they titrate down to the most effective dose,” says Heidi Skolnik, MS, CDN, nutritionist and author of Your GLP-1 Game Initiative. “You're trying to find what's the lowest amount that still is effective for you.”.

But what you don't want to do is eat a lot of high fat,” she says. “This is because your gastric system is slowing down. With high-fat foods, you may not digest all of that.”.

Sources indicate that not sure what’s high-fat or not? Play it safe and bring your own appetizer. Not only are you being a hospitable guest, but you’ll have something you can eat. Skolnik recommends:.

Recent findings suggest that so include those carb-heavy sides like mac and cheese and creamy mashed potatoes—just keep it to around a quarter of your plate. The majority of your plate should include a mix of vegetables and protein, which Skolnik says is usually manageable with turkey.

Recent findings suggest that common side effects of GLP-1 use include nausea from drinking and a reduced craving for alcohol. If you can tolerate one or two, both dietitians say to go for it. A drinking variation of the “Delicious to Me” strategy is the “9 Sips” rule. “You still need to factor in what sugar, caffeine, and alcohol will do but a smaller amount is the win while still enjoying,” says Koff. You’ll also want to drink water at regular intervals while you’re drinking.

If you want to avoid being pressured into drinking, Skolnik claims to also have a drink on hand with a lime slice to give the appearance of an alcoholic drink. “Nobody has to know what's in your glass.”.

It has been revealed that no need to ruin a favorite dessert by trying to choose only high-protein items. If you want to save your appetite for an extra slice of pie, Koff says to go for it. Just make sure to meet your nutritional needs in different ways as with a protein drink before dinner or supplements.

IT’S NOT JUST the food you need to navigate; the interactions matter too. Depending on your family situation, you may need to set some firm boundaries on or redirect comments related to your weight or appetite. That doesn’t mean the holidays are the time to announce to everyone you’re on a GLP-1 (unless you want to). Some phrases you can use include:.

In a recent development, skolnik claims having an ally is extremely important if you’re expecting other people to comment on your eating habits or your looks. They can help to redirect any uncomfortable conversation, provide support for your choices so you don’t feel isolated, or just provide emotional support. “Have someone else in the room with a code word or a look that signals them to intervene and change the conversation or divert attention away,” she says.

Even if you don’t have an ally physically next to you, have someone available on the phone that you can text or call. Skolnik says to escape to the bathroom if you need and use it as a place to recenter.

To avoid offending people who probably spent hours cooking, it can also be helpful to practice polite ways to turn down second helpings or pass on specific dishes.

“When the giving of food is looked at as love, the receiving of it is love,” indicates Skolnik. “But you can still receive the love without the food.”.

According to recent reports, rivian’s upcoming electric bike spinoff, ALSO, has hit another speed bump. The manufacturer has confirmed that it is temporarily halting deliveries of its TM-B electric bicycles after discovering software-related problems affecting some bikes, including issues with charging behavior.

And unfortunately, this isn’t entirely surprising. We’ve already reported on some strange battery behavior with the newly introduced e-bikes, as well as customers having to send their bikes back for repairs.

In a message sent to customers, ALSO explained that it was pausing shipments to address several software problems before more bikes reach riders.

“We’ve identified a few software-based issues, such as charging behavior, that are impacting some bikes,” the company explained.

ALSO claims its engineers are working on a firmware patch to resolve the problems, with shipments expected to resume in approximately two weeks.

The pause affects the remaining Launch Edition deliveries as well as the beginning of Performance Edition shipments, both of which will now arrive later than previously promised.

The announcement follows earlier reports of unusual charging and discharging behavior on the TM-B, which we previously highlighted as some of the growing pains facing Rivian’s ambitious upcoming e-bike venture.

We’ve also reported on customers needing to return their bikes for repairs, raising questions about how smoothly the company’s initial rollout was progressing.

The issues align with many of our initial concerns we discussed a year ago when the bike was first unveiled, namely that the high-tech design means the bike incorporates many new and proprietary systems that could each lead to complicated and costly failures.

Now ALSO has officially acknowledged software problems affecting some bikes, including charging behavior, though it hasn’t detailed the full extent of the issues or confirmed whether they are directly related to those earlier reports.

I love the PR spin how only "some" bikes are affected. If it's the same bike running the same software, it's affected. The only bikes not affected are the ones that haven't been delivered, because they are not being used.

The bike represents a fairly radical departure from traditional electric bicycles, with proprietary technology throughout its drivetrain and control systems. That makes software an especially vital part of the ownership experience.

It has been revealed that to ALSO’s credit, pausing deliveries to fix known problems is probably the right move. Nobody wants to receive a premium-priced electric bicycle only to discover that it needs an immediate trip back to the manufacturer.

But for customers who have already waited longer than expected, another delay is undoubtedly frustrating.

ALSO says it will provide another update on November 24, hopefully with better news about when deliveries can resume.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Less than 400 adult North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis) still exist in the wild, making them one of the world’s most critically endangered species.
  • In a recent development, “Naming right whales is a fun and creative activity for our research community, but it also allows an opportunity to connect with the whales on an individual level,” Amy Warren, an aquarium scientific program officer and name project coordinator, remarked in Anderson Cabot Center’s announcement.
  • The 2026 inductees also include Grand Slam (Catalog #3991) and Slide (Catalog #4991).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Less than 400 adult North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis) still exist in the wild, making them one of the world’s most critically endangered species. Of those, 20 have officially received spiffy new names from conservationists at the New England Aquarium’s Anderson Cabot Center for Ocean Life. The researchers curate the annual North Atlantic Right Whale Catalog, and attach personable monikers to a select few baleen cetaceans in order to more easily monitor them. This year, it’s time to wave hello to Dodo, Volcano, and Dolly.

In a recent development, “Naming right whales is a fun and creative activity for our research community, but it also allows an opportunity to connect with the whales on an individual level,” Amy Warren, an aquarium scientific program officer and name project coordinator, remarked in Anderson Cabot Center’s announcement. “It can be hard to relate to Catalog #5299, but a whale named Nibbles is bound to be memorable.”.

The 2026 inductees also include Grand Slam (Catalog #3991) and Slide (Catalog #4991). The sister whales have a mother named Fenway (Catalog #2791), who was also named in honor of the Boston Red Sox. Grand Slam earned her fresh name thanks to her three patches of raised tissue known as callosities that resemble the bases on a baseball field. Meanwhile, Slide received their name due to the curved scar on her back that recalls someone sliding through home plate. Other right whale names this year include Goose, Donegal, and even Gonzo for the beloved Muppet.

“Although the names are intended to help researchers at sea, they also give the general public a better understanding of the individual whales,” added Caroline Mowdy, a spokesperson for Whale and Dolphin Conservation (WDC).

Collaborators at the WDC also created some lighthearted, yearbook-esque biographies for each whale. For example, Dolly (Catalog #4191), whose callosity looks strikingly similar to the late, great country singer’s larger-than-life hair, apparently loves the song, “Jolene.” Then again, who doesn’t?

“We see these whales and their families grow each year,” said Mowdy. “Knowing them makes the tragedies even more tragic, but it also makes our determination to protect them even stronger.”.

It has been revealed that on Monday, the North Atlantic Right Whale Consortium announced that there are roughly 382 North Atlantic right whales, representing a 1.8 percent drop in population size from the 2024 estimate. Their primary threats remain getting tangled in fishing line and vessel strikes.

However, even amid their struggles, the 2025–2026 right whale calving season saw the most calves born since 2009. A total of 24 calves were born, including a surprising late addition that was spotted in Canada in September.

#75370. 6 Ways to Conquer Your Worst Fears

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1218 w)

6 Ways to Conquer Your Worst Fears

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1218 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 21, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • Life presents many reasons to worry and fret, but there is one that universally affects everyone.
  • An area of research in psychology that goes back several decades tackles this fear head-on.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 21, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

Life presents many reasons to worry and fret, but there is one that universally affects everyone. An inevitable aspect of life is that it will end, a reality that you face from the moment you’re old enough to realize death’s universality. The question is how much fear over this inevitability will interfere with your ability to appreciate what your life now has to offer.

An area of research in psychology that goes back several decades tackles this fear head-on. Death anxiety, as it is called, affects everyone, but to varying degrees. Why some people become obsessed with their mortality and others remain more placid over the whole matter is an concern at the heart of this field. Research and theories devoted to the understanding of death anxiety can provide insight into how to transform those who are obsessed with this fear into those who can approach their mortality with greater acceptance. A new paper by Holy Spirit of Kaslik (USEK)’s Ruth Younes and colleagues (2026) lays out the prominent theories of death anxiety, theories that can provide a guide to intervention.

One theory receiving the greatest empirical support is terror management theory (TMT), whose name states it all. We fear death, the theory proposes, because we live in “terror” of our mortality. However, we can’t live our lives continually in terror, so instead we “manage” the fear by suppressing it. Once in a while, though, that suppression stops working, and we face mortality head-on.

According to recent reports, A second theory has its origins in Erikson’s psychosocial approach to lifespan development. Erikson proposed that at any time in life, but especially in later adulthood, we take what Younes et al. call a “retrospective look-back on life.” If people are able to look back not in anger, but with satisfaction, they can cope more successfully with mortality than if they believe they failed. “Ego integrity,” the positive resolution of this issue, means that you view life, and the inevitability of death, with acceptance. “Despair,” the opposite, means that you see yourself as a failure and wish you could have a do-over to fix the mistakes you made when you were younger.

The third theory relevant to death anxiety is called gerotranscendence, and proposes that aging allows people to experience “transformative” shifts in their outlook on life. This occurs through the Cosmic dimension (deepening connection with the universe), the Self (unity and cohesion within the self), and Social/Personal relationship dimension (need for more selectiveness in social interactions). By developing these three qualities, individuals should experience less fear of death.

Through distilling the available literature, the USEK author team arrived at six common themes in interventions designed to mitigate death anxiety. They are as follows:.

Developed as an approach based on Erikson’s theory, reminiscence therapy uses the life review as its main tool. In life review, you return in time to the main events of your life and rework them from your present vantage point. Perhaps you jilted a lover who could have become your life partner by carelessly breaking things off over a silly argument. In retrospect, you ponder why you hurt this person so badly through this insensitivity. You can’t repair the damage, but you can gain perspective from your life as it unfolded since then. This breakup helped you learn to be kinder and to appreciate the importance of healing within close relationships.

According to recent reports, in this approach to therapy, people also relive their past, but they do so in an attempt to form an integrated “narrative” or story of their lives. Instead of reworking the past as in reminiscence therapy, you attempt to come back into awareness of it. As you do so, your life takes on shape and meaning. For example, you might try to prompt your recall of such events as the birth of your children and their early development up to the present. This allows you to piece back together events that you may have forgotten simply because your life was so busy at the time, balancing work and family demands.

According to recent reports, instead of rehashing the lows and highs of past events in your life, you might try instead to focus on the highs. This could be useful if reminiscence proves too painful. By starting with the positive, you can eventually confront the negative. Regarding yourself as someone who made good decisions in life, you may then approach the times you didn’t with greater self-compassion.

This might not be something you should “try at home,” but insights from the way that psychodynamic theory works could be useful. Younes et al. mention, for example, the “grieving” process that people experience as they think about the end of their lives. Research on end-of-life concerns suggests that people engage in anticipatory grief about their own lives as a way to come to greater acceptance. If you run from this form of grief, as TMT might suggest, it could come back to haunt you when you come much closer to your life’s end.

5. Acceptance and Commitment Therapy.

Recent findings suggest that this is a form of therapy used for a number of psychological disorders in which an individual learns to accept distressing events and pain without avoidance. The “commitment” piece of this involves setting and acting toward your goals. Rather than run away from thoughts of death, you would therefore confront them and reflect on how you can live your life according to your values.

6. Dialectical Behavior Therapy.

Sources indicate that an approach used in the treatment of people with borderline personality disorder (invented by the late Marsha Linehan), this therapy involves accepting your feelings and behaviors while also trying to change your behaviors. Again, you may not be able to do this on your own as a formal therapy, but the idea of rethinking your feelings and behaviors is very doable.

Each of the six ways of addressing death anxiety takes a slightly different slant on the processes of reflecting back on your life, reworking some old complications, and tackling fears of death through acceptance. The authors suggest that people vary in which approach works best for them.

Sources indicate that additional factors from the study that might influence the way you go about trying these yourself or with someone close to you include your age and health. A health scare, such as an acute cardiac event or bad news from a screening test, can set anyone off, regardless of age. On the other hand, social support can help you get through these and other tough times as you confront your feelings about mortality.

According to recent reports, to sum up, death anxiety stems from the inevitability of our own mortality, but it need not be an inevitable feature of your mental health. Being able to recognize and work through these feelings can prepare you for whatever lies ahead.

Younes, R. S., Rahme, E., Rajha, F., & Abboud Mzawak, M. (2026). Exploring death anxiety among older adults: An integrative review of associated factors and interventions. Omega: Journal of Death and Dying, 93(3), 1799–1829. https://doi.org/10.1177/00302228241272578.

How To Build Strength You’ll Actually Use In Daily Life, According To A Trainer

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (660 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Womenshealthmag

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Strength training isn't just about what you can lift in the gym.
  • As we get older, we naturally start to lose muscle mass, strength and bone density—at approximately 3-8% per decade after the age of 30—but regular strength training can help slow this down, reminds Andy Carr, trainer and head of fitness for Snap Fitness UK.
  • Thankfully, you don't need complicated exercises to see the benefits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Strength training isn't just about what you can lift in the gym. It helps make everyday tasks easier, whether that's carrying heavy shopping bags and moving furniture or putting a suitcase in the overhead compartment on a flight.

As we get older, we naturally start to lose muscle mass, strength and bone density—at approximately 3-8% per decade after the age of 30—but regular strength training can help slow this down, reminds Andy Carr, trainer and head of fitness for Snap Fitness UK.

Thankfully, you don't need complicated exercises to see the benefits.

By focusing on simple, functional movements that mimic everyday activities, you can build strength that carries over into daily life and keeps you strong, active and confident as you get older.

Sources indicate that “It's not necessary to spend hours lifting weights to build strength that makes a difference,” he explains. “Even two or three strength sessions a week can help, especially when you're focusing on compound exercises that work several muscle groups at once.”.

Squats are one of the best exercises for building lower-body strength because—as a compound exercise—they work your thighs, glutes, and core all at once.

Industry observers note that “These are the muscles you use when getting up from a chair, lifting something off the floor or crouching down to do some gardening,” states Carr. Keeping them strong can make a real difference to how easily you move around, particularly as you get older.

Step-ups are great for building leg strength and improving balance at the same time, says Carr.

It has been revealed that “They're particularly useful for everyday activities like climbing stairs, walking uphill, or stepping onto curbs. As we age, maintaining strength and stability in our legs becomes increasingly crucial, and step-ups are a simple way to work on both,” he adds.

Farmer's carries are a brilliant exercise for building strength you actually use, because they're essentially the same movement as carrying heavy shopping bags.

It has been revealed that “They work your grip, shoulders and core, helping you carry things more comfortably and with better stability. Grip strength can decline with age, so it's a really useful exercise to include in your routine,” indicates Carr.

Recent findings suggest that picking something up, whether it's a laundry basket, a suitcase or a bag of compost in the garden, involves your glutes, hamstrings, and back. Deadlifts strengthen all these muscles, explains Carr.

“They're a great way to build strength for everyday lifting, so those jobs feel easier and you're more confident handling heavier objects.”.

Rows are ideal for strengthening your upper back and arms, which we use for pulling movements throughout the day, from opening heavy doors to pulling a garden hose across the lawn.

It has been revealed that “They also help support good posture, particularly if you spend a lot of time sitting at a desk,” claims Carr. “Using a resistance band makes it easy to adjust the difficulty as you get stronger.”.

Incline push-ups are a great way to build upper-body strength, working your chest, shoulders, arms, and core.

“These muscles help with everyday pushing movements, whether that's moving a shopping cart, pushing open a heavy door, or getting yourself up from the floor,” claims Carr.

They're also easy to adapt to your fitness level, so you can gradually increase the challenge as your strength improves.

We use rotational movements more than we probably realize, whether that's turning to put something in the back of the car, reaching across to pick something up or digging in the garden.

Woodchops are great for strengthening your core and improving your ability to twist and turn with control, Carr explains.

“That becomes particularly useful as we get older, helping us stay mobile and making everyday movements feel easier.”.

Tech Report: Genesis Is Trying to Bring Its 1100-HP X-Scorpio SUV Concept to Production, Hyundai CEO Says

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (494 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that genesis might be a carmaker that has so far largely stuck to meat-and-potatoes models like sedans and SUVs, but the Korean luxury brand has also pumped out quite a few tantalizing concept cars in recent years.
  • Industry observers note that “We are working with designers to try to put [the X-Scorpio] into the market,” Muñoz told AN.
  • It has been revealed that if the X-Scorpio does reach showrooms, it would mark yet another flank in the Hyundai Motor Group’s fast-moving and wide-ranging onslaught of off-road trucks and SUVs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that genesis might be a carmaker that has so far largely stuck to meat-and-potatoes models like sedans and SUVs, but the Korean luxury brand has also pumped out quite a few tantalizing concept cars in recent years. Some of them, like the G90 Wingback and Magma GT supercar, have seemed almost production-ready; others, like the X Gran Equator and X-Scorpio off-roaders, less so. But according to Automotive News, the wild X-Scorpio concept could in fact wind up in showrooms—and none other than Hyundai CEO Jose Muñoz is the one spreading the news.

Industry observers note that “We are working with designers to try to put [the X-Scorpio] into the market,” Muñoz told AN. The feedback that Genesis received from dealers and potential customers was so positive, he mentioned, that “we are going to give it a try.”.

It has been revealed that if the X-Scorpio does reach showrooms, it would mark yet another flank in the Hyundai Motor Group’s fast-moving and wide-ranging onslaught of off-road trucks and SUVs. Hyundai and Kia have both made clear plans for multiple body-on-frame vehicles, including ones inspired by the Hyundai Boulder concept revealed at this year’s Upcoming York Auto Show; Genesis itself, meanwhile, has confirmed the luxurious X Gran Equator will enter production, potentially rivaling everything from the Lexus LX to the Mercedes-Benz G-wagen.

According to recent reports, still, none of those are anything like the X-Scorpio. In fact, there’s nothing quite like it on sale today, period. The concept, at least, is something of a cross between a Local Motors Rally Fighter and a Lamborghini Huracan Sterrato, with a twin-turbo V-8 putting out 1100 horsepower and 850 pound-feet of torque that gets sent to 40-inch off-road tires on 18-inch beadlock wheels. It was designed, the organization says, for the Middle East, where screaming across open terrain and sending it off sand dunes is, as the press release politely puts it, “a favorite pastime”—but considering how those are also quite popular here in the United States (see: TRX, Ram; Raptor, Ford), it seems likely a production X-Scorpio would also be a hit here.

According to recent reports, of course, talk is cheap, even if it’s an automotive CEO saying it. Genesis does indeed have massive plans for a bunch of newly introduced cars over the next few years, with 22 all-new or revised models coming by 2030. But whether there’s room on the balance sheet to develop for a bespoke off-road sports car with no direct competitors seems like a fairly large question mark, so let’s just keep our fingers crossed for now.

#75367. Tesla toughens FSD driver monitoring in Europe while loosening it in the US

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1130 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Tesla toughens FSD driver monitoring in Europe while loosening it in the US

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1130 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla is rolling out stricter driver monitoring for its “Full Self-Driving” system in Europe, with earlier warnings, a full strike for drivers who look away during a manoeuvre, and a hands-on-wheel requirement above 130 km/h (81 mph).
  • In the US, Tesla has spent the last year going the other way.
  • Recent findings suggest that on November 16, the Dutch vehicle authority RDW announced that it signed off on a latest update to Tesla Assisted Driving, the name Tesla now uses for FSD (Supervised) in Europe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla is rolling out stricter driver monitoring for its “Full Self-Driving” system in Europe, with earlier warnings, a full strike for drivers who look away during a manoeuvre, and a hands-on-wheel requirement above 130 km/h (81 mph).

In the US, Tesla has spent the last year going the other way. Its CEO told owners they can text and drive on FSD, and recent US builds were tuned to nag drivers less.

Recent findings suggest that on November 16, the Dutch vehicle authority RDW announced that it signed off on a latest update to Tesla Assisted Driving, the name Tesla now uses for FSD (Supervised) in Europe. It covers HW4 vehicles and goes out over the air.

According to the RDW, drivers now get attention warnings earlier. If a driver isn’t paying attention while the system performs a manoeuvre, they get a “full strike.” The regulator says the patch also adds measures to prevent misuse of the system, but it didn’t spell out what they are.

It has been revealed that there’s a speed component too. Above 130 km/h (where legal), the driver has to keep their hands on the wheel. And setting a maximum speed above what the system displays now requires the driver to confirm it by scrolling the wheel up, with the speed limit sign pulsing red when the car goes over.

Recent findings suggest that the RDW says it tested the revision on its own track and on public roads and found no adverse or unintended effects. Ten other countries have adopted the Dutch approval so far, with Finland now on the list, while EU-wide approval is still waiting on a vote at the TCMV, the committee of member states.

Sources indicate that this comes two weeks after Tesla cut the system’s speed margin from 50% to 10% over the limit in Europe and dropped the “Full Self-Driving” name there. Germany had made both a condition of supporting EU approval.

Now look at how Tesla handles the same software at home.

In a recent development, at Tesla’s shareholder meeting last November, Musk complained that the car was “a little strict about keeping your eyes on the road” and said Tesla would “allow you to text and drive essentially” within a month or two. A month later, an owner asked whether FSD v14.2.1 allowed texting. Musk’s answer: “Depending on context of surrounding traffic, yes.”.

Texting while driving is illegal in 49 states. FSD is still a Level 2 system, and Tesla’s own fine print says the driver is responsible at all times.

According to recent reports, in May, Musk confirmed that FSD v14.3.3 was built to nag drivers less. Tesla did add better eye-gaze tracking and eyewear handling in a June build, to be fair. But the pitch to owners hasn’t changed: fewer nags is sold as a feature.

Industry observers note that and US drivers have been allowed to go hands-free on FSD at any speed since Tesla moved to cabin-camera monitoring in 2024. There’s no 130 km/h rule here.

NHTSA noticed. In its engineering analysis of FSD crashes in low-visibility conditions, the agency asked Tesla to justify a list of its marketing claims, and it specifically cited Musk’s texting post. In September, Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi asked NHTSA to look into Tesla’s driver monitoring after dozens of videos appeared to show drivers asleep on Autopilot and FSD.

Recent findings suggest that the results are on the road. Last month, a driver told the CHP he was asleep on FSD when his Tesla drove through a freeway closure and hit a patrol car, seriously injuring two officers. Owners are also filming themselves defeating Tesla’s driver monitoring and posting it for clout.

Both markets get the same cabin camera and the same HW4 computer.

It has been revealed that but in Europe, a type-approval authority tests every update before it ships and can refuse it. In the US, nobody pre-approves driver-assist software. Tesla self-certifies, and NHTSA only steps in after complaints and crashes pile up, which is how you end up with a CEO publicly telling owners to text while the regulator is still writing letters about it.

This revision proves Tesla can build stricter driver monitoring whenever a regulator demands it. The code exists. It’s running on HW4 cars in 11 European countries right now.

That's because Musk is buddies with the current federal government that would regulate his not-full-self-driving system. Whereas Europe doesn't kowtow to his whims. We'll see what happens in 2029 with a fresh administration.

That makes the US approach hard to defend. Tesla’s argument for relaxing supervision is that FSD is now good enough. But if that were true, it would be showing the RDW data proving looser monitoring is safe, not adding earlier warnings and harsher strikes to get approved. It’s doing the opposite in Europe because it has to, and the opposite of that in the US because it can.

According to recent reports, we’ve been saying it for a while: FSD gets more dangerous as it gets better, because people trust it more and watch the road less. The answer is monitoring that tightens as the system improves. Europe is forcing exactly that. In the US, Tesla is loosening it, encouraging illegal phone use from the top, and leaving drivers with 100% of the liability when it goes wrong.

So here’s the question for Tesla. If European owners are getting earlier warnings and instant strikes, why not American owners on the exact same software? Or is NHTSA going to have to force it?
